paragraphs: Photographers photograph people, landscapes, products, or other subjects, design lighting and composition, and use editing software to deliver images or photographs. Photographers photograph people, landscapes, products, or other subjects, design lighting and composition, and use editing software to deliver images or photographs. They check client briefs, subjects, lighting, original images, permissions, and delivery specifications and deliver traceable originals, selections, retouched versions, and images for their intended uses. Consent of people depicted, location permits, copyright, usage scope, and image authenticity must be checked against project agreements and applicable law.
O*NET 27-4021.00 is a separate US photographer profile; occupational definitions, tasks, interests, and work styles do not equal Chinese occupational qualifications or recruitment requirements.

paragraphs:
Settings | Studios, client sites, outdoor locations, or news scenes.
Objects | Client briefs, subjects, lighting, original images, permissions, and delivery specifications.
Tasks | Photograph people, landscapes, products, or other subjects, design lighting and composition, and use editing software to deliver images or photographs.
Collaboration | Communicate with clients, subjects, stylists, editors, and production teams.
Time | Projects, weather, locations, or event times affect work arrangements.
Quality | Traceable originals, selections, retouched versions, and images delivered for their intended uses must be reviewable.
Information | Use only authorized materials and protect privacy.
Risks | Pause or escalate when portrait or location permissions are insufficient, images are distorted, files are lost, delivery specifications are wrong, or on-site safety issues arise.
Boundaries | Consent of people depicted, location permits, copyright, usage scope, and image authenticity must be checked against project agreements and applicable law.

O*NET lists photographing people, landscapes, products, or other subjects, designing lighting and composition, and using editing software to deliver images or photographs; the specific work mix varies by institution and position. An occupational classification cannot directly replace local entry requirements.

The BLS photographer OOH describes shooting, editing, portfolios, and self-employed business operations; part-time work is common, evenings and weekends may be required, and work may involve standing, walking, or carrying heavy equipment.

Check inputs and sources → Confirm task scope → Photograph people, landscapes, products, or other subjects, design lighting and composition, and use editing software to deliver images or photographs → Compare client briefs, subjects, lighting, original images, permissions, and delivery specifications → Address insufficient portrait or location permissions, image distortion, lost files, incorrect delivery specifications, or on-site safety issues → Deliver and document traceable originals, selections, retouched versions, and images for their intended uses.

China's GB/T 4754—2017 classifies 8060 photographic and photofinishing services under residential services, repairs, and other services. In 2025, this industry's pretax average annual wages were CNY 70,226 in urban nonprivate units and CNY 52,059 in private units; match the employer's main activity. These are not a national photographer median.

When insufficient portrait or location permissions, image distortion, lost files, incorrect delivery specifications, or on-site safety issues are found, pause affected steps, preserve original evidence and versions, and refer the matter to authorized personnel.

US EP Table 1.2 lists photographer employment of 145,000 in 2025 and a projected 144,000 in 2035, a net decline of 1,000 and a decrease of 0.7%, with average annual openings of 10,700 including replacements; typical entry education is high school or equivalent, with moderate-term on-the-job training. These are not Chinese education requirements.

Confirm tasks and scope → Check client briefs, subjects, lighting, original images, permissions, and delivery specifications → Produce an initial draft → Create traceable originals, selections, retouched versions, and images for their intended uses → Review evidence and limitations → Hand over.

When handling images of identifiable people, check the applicable basis, purpose, and necessary scope under China's Personal Information Protection Law; not every photograph is sensitive personal information. Portrait use and copyright in photographic works also require separate checks under the Civil Code and Copyright Law.
The handover sheet lists sources, versions, subjects, anomalies, work completed and not completed, the recipient, and next steps.

Photographers mainly deliver still photographs; camera operators record continuous footage, editors organize moving images and sound, and graphic designers create graphics. Shared equipment or editing skills do not confer automatic mutual recognition of job responsibilities.
Camera operators record scenes through shots and continuous action; a still portfolio cannot replace a video sample.
Use lighting, composition, and exposure to create still images serving specific purposes.
Adjacent editors work with moving images and audio tracks; designers work with layouts, graphics, and commercial communication needs.
The main objects are subjects, client needs, originals, and delivery specifications; check fidelity, selections, and dimensions when editing.

Photographers photograph people, products, landscapes, and other subjects, creating still images through lighting, exposure, and composition, and selecting and editing photographs; they may produce traditional or digital photographs. Specific tasks vary across portrait, commercial, news, or scientific photography.
Film and video editors create finished works through shot sequencing, rhythm, and audiovisual synchronization; photographic postproduction does not equal full video production.
Set aperture, shutter speed, and focus, arrange lights or use reflectors, then select, retouch, archive, and deliver photographs after shooting.
Camera operators deliver continuous footage, editors deliver edited moving images, and graphic designers deliver graphic designs.

Deliver selected photographs, images exported for intended uses, and originals and edited versions that must be retained; original file delivery and copyright arrangements depend separately on the contract.
Adjacent positions are responsible for their respective recording, editing, or design tasks; the project confirms team responsibilities.
Photographers shoot, select images, and deliver; self-employed photographers may also handle client acquisition, bookings, bookkeeping, billing, and employee management.
Owning a camera, completing a photography course, or using retouching software cannot replace permission for a specific use.
Check portrait rights, rights in works, and contractual usage scope; assess exceptions permitted by Chinese law according to their conditions, without claiming that every shoot requires consent.

US occupational data, individual employer recruitment requirements, and Chinese industry averages measure different things and cannot establish the same person's entry requirements, pay, or unemployment risk.

Before starting, check settings, education and portfolios, equipment, postproduction delivery, rights arrangements, and contractual income structure; the following six items are checking suggestions.
Shooting setting
Confirm portrait, product, news, scientific, or another direction; check on-site work, travel, seasons, and shifts.
Education and portfolio

Typical US entry education is high school or equivalent, with moderate-term on-the-job training; some employers require or prefer a related bachelor's degree. Check specific Chinese notices separately.
Equipment and site
Confirm who provides cameras, lenses, lights, and backup media; check handling, wiring, and location safety.
Editing and export
Confirm selections, retouching, color, file formats, and delivery quantities; check authenticity rules separately for news or evidentiary uses.
Rights and publication
Separately check portrait use, rights in commissioned or employment-related works, display channels, and territorial and time limits; do not expand unclear rights without authorization.
Remuneration and business operations
Check employment or project contracts, pay units, equipment and travel costs, and copyright usage fees; self-employed order revenue is not wage survey income.

subject.name: Photographers
subject.summary: Photographers (O*NET 27-4021.00) photograph people, landscapes, products, or other subjects, design lighting and composition, and use editing software to deliver images or photographs. Working with client briefs, subjects, lighting, original images, permissions, and delivery specifications, they produce traceable originals, selections, retouched versions, and images delivered for their intended uses. Consent of people depicted, location permits, copyright, usage scope, and image authenticity must be checked against project agreements and applicable law. Work settings, qualifications, and final responsibility must be checked against local and institutional rules.
